text:
Give Mira a heads-up before you leave, not a surprise. At 26 months, big feelings still outpace the words to handle them, so an abrupt exit tips her over — the Child Development & Wellbeing Companion frames this as a transition skill she's still building, not defiance.

A few things that help:

- Two warnings: "five more minutes," then "one more slide, then shoes."
- A closing ritual — wave bye to the swings, count the steps to the gate.
- Name the feeling on the way out: "you're sad to leave. We'll come back."

Some days she'll melt down anyway. Staying calm and consistent beats negotiating at the gate, and it does ease as she gets more practice.
